The **Akashi Kaikyo Bridge** ([Japanese](/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language"): 明石海峡大橋, [Hepburn](/wiki/Hepburn_romanization "Hepburn romanization"): *Akashi Kaikyō Ōhashi*) is a [suspension bridge](/wiki/Suspension_bridge "Suspension bridge") that links the city of [Kobe](/wiki/Kobe "Kobe") on the Japanese island of [Honshu](/wiki/Honshu "Honshu") and [Iwaya, Awaji](/w/index.php?title=Iwaya,_Awaji&action=edit&redlink=1 "Iwaya, Awaji (page does not exist)") [[ja](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%B2%A9%E5%B1%8B%E7%94%BA "ja:岩屋町")] on [Awaji Island](/wiki/Awaji_Island "Awaji Island"). It was completed in 1998,[[1]](#cite_note-structurae-1) and at the time, was the [longest central span of any suspension bridge](/wiki/List_of_longest_suspension_bridge_spans "List of longest suspension bridge spans") in the world,[[4]](#cite_note-hsbe-4) at 1,991 metres (6,532 ft). From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge1.JPG/330px-1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge1.JPG)](/wiki/File:1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge1.JPG)

The [1915 Çanakkale Bridge](/wiki/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge "1915 Çanakkale Bridge") in Turkey, opened in 2022, has the longest central span (2,023 m) of any suspension bridge.[[1]](#cite_note-The_B1M-1)[[2]](#cite_note-B1M-website-2)[[3]](#cite_note-HDN-3) It crosses the [Dardanelles](/wiki/Dardanelles "Dardanelles") in Turkey.

The world's **longest suspension bridges** are listed according to the length of their main [span](/wiki/Span_(architecture) "Span (architecture)") (i.e., the length of suspended roadway between the bridge's towers). The length of the main span is the most common method of comparing the sizes of [suspension bridges](/wiki/Suspension_bridge "Suspension bridge"), often correlating with the height of the towers and the engineering complexity involved in designing and constructing the bridge.[[4]](#cite_note-4) If one bridge has a longer span than another, it does not necessarily mean that the bridge is longer from shore to shore (or from [abutment](/wiki/Abutment "Abutment") to abutment).

Suspension bridges have the longest spans of any type of bridge. [Cable-stayed bridges](/wiki/Cable-stayed_bridge "Cable-stayed bridge"), the next longest design, are practical for spans up to just over one kilometre (the [longest cable-stayed bridge in the world](/wiki/Russky_Bridge "Russky Bridge") has a 1,104 m span). Therefore, as of October 2025, the 28 longest bridges on this list are the 28 longest spans of all types of vehicular bridges (other than floating [pontoon bridges](/wiki/Pontoon_bridge "Pontoon bridge")).

The [1915 Çanakkale Bridge](/wiki/1915_%C3%87anakkale_Bridge "1915 Çanakkale Bridge") in Turkey holds the record since opening to traffic in March 2022, with a span of 2,023 metres (6,637 ft).[[1]](#cite_note-The_B1M-1)[[3]](#cite_note-HDN-3) Since 1998, the [Akashi Kaikyo Bridge](/wiki/Akashi_Kaikyo_Bridge "Akashi Kaikyo Bridge") in Japan previously held the record with a span of 1,991 metres (6,532 feet), the [Zhangjinggao Yangtze River Bridge](/wiki/Zhangjinggao_Yangtze_River_Bridge "Zhangjinggao Yangtze River Bridge") in [China](/wiki/China "China") will break the record in 2028 while the [Strait of Messina Bridge](/wiki/Strait_of_Messina_Bridge "Strait of Messina Bridge") in [Italy](/wiki/Italy "Italy") will go to the top of the list in 2032.

The bridge that held the world record for the longest suspension span just before the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge was the **Humber Bridge** in the United Kingdom.

*   **Context:** The Humber Bridge held the record from its opening in 1981 until the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge opened in 1998.
